tagline: One volcano and a string of islets
overview:
Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is a Caribbean country made of one main mountainous island, Saint Vincent, and a chain of about 30 smaller islands and cays called the Grenadines trailing southwest toward Grenada. The total land area is only about 389 km², but the islands are spread over a long stretch of clear blue sea.

About 110,000 people live here, nearly all on Saint Vincent itself. English is the official language, and a Vincentian creole is spoken every day. Kingstown, the capital, is a working port town of arched stone shopfronts beneath steep green hills.

The country is a constitutional monarchy with an elected parliament. Bananas and arrowroot were long the main crops, and tourism, especially sailing among the Grenadines, has grown. The active volcano La Soufrière looms over the north of the main island and erupted as recently as 2021.
landAndNature: Saint Vincent is steep, volcanic and wet, with a forested ridge running its length and La Soufrière, 1,234 meters high, at the northern end. Its 2021 eruption sent ash across the Caribbean and forced about 20,000 people from their homes. Black sand beaches line the windward side, and the Vermont Nature Trail in the rainforest is the place to look for the Saint Vincent parrot, a bronze, blue and gold bird found nowhere else and shown on the coat of arms. The Grenadines are lower and drier, fringed with white sand and coral: the Tobago Cays sit inside a horseshoe reef where green turtles graze on sea grass, and Mustique and Bequia are known for sailing and boatbuilding.
peopleAndCulture: Most Vincentians descend from enslaved Africans, with Indigenous Kalinago and Garifuna, Indian and Portuguese heritage also in the mix. Roasted breadfruit with fried jackfish is the national dish, and callaloo soup and rotis are everyday food. Vincy Mas, the carnival that peaks in early July, fills Kingstown with steel pan, soca, calypso competitions and masquerade bands. Bequia has a long whaling and boatbuilding tradition and is famous for model boats built by hand. Cricket is the leading sport, and Vincentians play for the West Indies team. Nine Mornings, a Christmas custom found nowhere else, has people rising before dawn for nine days of street dancing, swimming and concerts before sunrise.
history: Kalinago people held Saint Vincent longer than almost any other Caribbean island, resisting European settlement into the 1700s. Shipwrecked and escaped Africans joined them, forming the Garifuna, or Black Caribs. Britain gained the island in 1763, and after two wars the Garifuna were defeated in 1796 and about 5,000 were deported to an island off Honduras, from where their descendants spread along the Central American coast. Sugar estates worked by enslaved Africans dominated until slavery ended in 1834. In 1902 La Soufrière erupted catastrophically, killing about 1,600 people on the same day as the Mont Pelée disaster on Martinique. Saint Vincent and the Grenadines became fully independent on October 27, 1979, just months after another eruption of the volcano.
funFacts: Parts of the first Pirates of the Caribbean film were shot on Saint Vincent, and some set pieces remain at Wallilabou Bay.
During Nine Mornings, Vincentians get up before dawn for nine days in December to dance, swim and watch concerts.
The Tobago Cays are a group of uninhabited islands inside a horseshoe reef, where sea turtles feed in shallow water.
The world's oldest botanical garden in the Western Hemisphere, founded in Kingstown in 1765, still grows a breadfruit tree descended from Captain Bligh's plants.
La Soufrière's 2021 eruption blanketed the island in ash and forced about a fifth of the population to evacuate.
